READY for review: head `cb5c1f796dac6851062af69def634aade161fb1f` (read from the API after the push). It is one commit on main `1b0325719dd4a7a85a64dcdde749211332453425` and is not armed.

### Checks on m1 (sy-1.97.1, the rust-toolchain pin; nice, -j4, ulimit -Su, timeout, stdin /dev/null)
The tested tree is byte-identical to the committed source (`cmp` on every source file, and an identical `shasum` digest of the fixture directory). The two SKILL.md notes were added after the run and are documentation only.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`: exit 0. The only warning is the known `unknown lint: clippy::assert_is_empty`, which main also has.
- `cargo test --locked --lib -- gate_cost metrics_gate_cost`: 34 passed, 0 failed. That is 12 scorecard tests plus the existing gate-cost tests.
- Full suite, `--no-fail-fast` with `RUST_MIN_STACK=32MiB` (both main and branch overflow `branch_cmd::cli_surface_parses_branch_apply_create` at the default stack size):
  - Branch: 4085 passed, 35 failed. Main `1b0325719dd4a7a85a64dcdde749211332453425`: 4073 passed, 34 failed.
  - 34 of the failures are identical to main's (environmental on m1).
  - The 35th is `zero_job_recover::apply_spends_remote_receipt_then_dispatches_once_without_cancellation`. It reaches the real `~/.local/bin/ghapp` from an unsandboxed run, and main fails it the same way here. The #780 reviewer found it passes 19/19 on main inside a sandbox.
- Non-Rust pre-push gates, run by hand before pushing with `SHIPYARD_SKIP_PREPUSH=1`: skill_sync_check 0, version_bump_check 0, doc_sync_check 0, check_test_include_str 0.

### Mutants
Each is a non-empty 1/1 diff (1/0 for S9), run with `cargo test --locked --lib -- gate_cost::scorecard`. Afterwards each file was restored from pristine and checked with `cmp`, and `diff -rq` showed the whole tree pristine.

All 16 were killed. S14 survived the first time; `a_short_read_of_a_commit_s_checks_is_refused` was added for it.

### Live run, before and after 2026-10-11
I built the release binary on m1 and ran it read-only (`--no-cache`) from each repository's checkout, over 2026-09-28T00:00Z..2026-10-12T06:00Z.

**Control.** The pulp merged-PR counts match `search/issues` `total_count` exactly for each week (406 / 457 / 18), and the merge-group run counts match the workflow-runs `total_count` (506 / 603). One more control: the live run of the 2026-10-05 15:00..15:20 window prints the same numbers as the captured-fixture test.

| Repo, week | Merged | Open to merge median / p90 h | Ejections (gate failed) / gated runs | Run failed with gate green | Red after push | Top repeat failures (PRs) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pulp W40 | 406 | 1.36 / 8.67 | 49 (48) / 506 = 0.10 | 274 | 114/615 = 0.19 | Diff coverage advisory 391, Request Codex review 330, ASan 254, macos (required) 32 |
| pulp W41 | 457 | 1.94 / 11.61 | 59 (48, starved 10) / 603 = 0.10 | 146 | 135/782 = 0.17 | Diff coverage advisory 422, ASan 190, UBSan 128, macos (required) 32 |
| pulp W42 (to 06:00Z) | 18 | 11.46 / 29.1 | 6 (6) / 24 = 0.25 | 0 | 14/76 = 0.18 | Diff coverage advisory 16, Enforce version & skill sync (required) 4 |
| tartci W40 | 82 | 0.46 / 3.93 | no queue | | 9/151 = 0.06 | lint (required) 9 |
| tartci W41 | 91 | 0.92 / 16.67 | no queue | | 25/243 = 0.10 | lint (required) 16, python-39-tests 12 |
| Shipyard W40 | 69 | 2.46 / 21.55 | no queue | | 34/221 = 0.15\* | Windows 18, Enforce 14, macOS ARM64 [local] 13 |
| Shipyard W41 | 49 | 3.03 / 16.1 | no queue | | 89/295 = 0.30\* | version-ahead-of-main 21, Linux 17, Windows 15 |

- Pulp W41 lists `capped_prs` #9516 and #9755 (more than 250 commits).
- The pulp run reports a gap: the `merge_group` event walk could not reach back to the window start. So a filtered listing that GitHub shortened without saying so (the case gate-cost's cross-check exists for) would go unnoticed for this window. The per-week totals above do match GitHub's `total_count`.
- \*Shipyard has no branch protection, so these rates use `--required-context` with its four test legs. One of my four names, `macOS ARM64 [github-hosted]`, matches no check, and the report says so in a `required_contexts` gap. That is the guard working on live data; the other three are counted.

W42 holds 6 hours, which is too few for any verdict. These numbers are the baseline the P0 items are to be measured against.

Review of head cb5c1f796dac6851062af69def634aade161fb1f, done by recomputing the numbers. I read the head from the API before and after this review, and it is not armed.

**Independent recompute of Pulp ISO week 41** (2026-10-05T00:00Z..2026-10-12T00:00Z). I read GitHub through REST and GraphQL with my own scripts, not this PR's code.

| Metric | #784 evidence | My recompute | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Merged PRs | 457 | 457 (REST `search/issues`, one slice per day) | match |
| Open to merge, median / p90 h | 1.94 / 11.61 | 1.94 / 11.61 (same linear interpolation) | match |
| merge_group `build.yml` runs | 603 | 603 (`total_count` 603) | match |
| `macos` gate classes | 48 gate_failed, 10 starved, 1 cancelled after start; 146 run failed with gate green | 48 / 10 / 1; 146 | match |
| Red after push | 135/782 = 0.17 | 135/782 when GitHub's own `statusCheckRollup` is read with the PR's latest-of-each-name rule. Check runs alone give 109/782. The 26 extra are commits whose `Vellum trusted freeze` check run is SKIPPED but a later commit *status* of the same name from `github-actions[bot]` is `failure` ("base and head do not merge cleanly"). Protection pins that context to app 15368, and GitHub counts such a status, so 135 is right under the stated definition. | match |
| Capped PRs | #9516, #9755 | #9516, #9755. Live GraphQL for #9755 returns 250 nodes of `totalCount` 300. | match |
| Required `macos` red on ≥2 PRs | 32 | 32 | match |

**Fixtures are real.** I compared each against the live API: 5 search nodes (`createdAt` and `mergedAt`), 5 merge_group runs (head_branch, head_sha, event, created_at, run_attempt, conclusion), 5 `macos` jobs (conclusion, runner_name, started_at, completed_at, run_attempt) and 6 PR commit lists. **0 mismatches.** The two `contexts-*.json` commits have 100 and 102 live check runs, so the >100-checks page is exercised on real data.

**Pagination.**
- `gh --paginate` follows the first `pageInfo` in output order, which is the commits connection, not the nested contexts.
- Contexts beyond 100 are re-read by `read_contexts` with an exact `totalCount` check.
- The 250-commit cap is counted and reported, never silently truncated.
- Partial search, run and commit reads are refused.

**Must-fix: "ejection rate" does not measure ejections.** GitHub records every queue removal as a `RemovedFromMergeQueueEvent` with a reason. Reading those for all 467 PRs that W41 merge_group runs reference, W41 had **38 check-based ejections** by `github-merge-queue`: 36 `failed_checks` and 2 `checks_timed_out`. There were also 17 `merge_conflict`, 27 `manual` by shipyard-local, 5 `manual` by the queue and 1 by danielraffel. The scorecard reports **59 ejections, a rate of 0.10**. Matching each run to the PR's next event:
- Of the 59 counted runs, only **24** are followed by a check-based removal of that PR.
  - **32** (25 gate_failed and 7 starved) had **no removal** before the PR's next merge-group run. The group failed or was cancelled because a batch-mate or a rebuild invalidated it, and the PR stayed queued.
  - 3 ended in a manual removal.
- Of the 38 real check-based ejections, **13 happened while `build.yml`'s `macos` gate passed**. Another of Pulp's six required contexts ejected the PR: the Vellum freezes, drift-fast, Enforce or Build+prove. 1 more had no build run. So "a merge-group run that failed while its gate passed is not an ejection" is correct only for a queue with one required context. On Pulp it drops real ejections.
- `cancelled` gates are always counted, as `starved` or `cancelled_after_start`, but a group cancelled by a queue rebuild is not an ejection.

Fix: count ejections from the timeline. Count `RemovedFromMergeQueueEvent` with actor `github-merge-queue` and reason `failed_checks` or `checks_timed_out`, report `merge_conflict` and `manual` apart, and use queue entries (`AddedToMergeQueueEvent`) as the denominator. Keep the per-run gate classification as a separate, honestly named metric, "merge-group gate failure rate". Add a fixture pair from W41 for each disagreement class, and fix the definition in `--help` and the module docs.

**Should-fix:** red after push judges all six required contexts, but the ejection side reads only `--gate-job` in one workflow. The report should say which contexts each rate covers.

**CI on this head.** Linux ×3, Windows ×2, macOS ARM64 [github-hosted], Coverage ×2, Python helper tests ×2, Enforce version & skill sync ×2 and Resolve runners ×3 are all `success`. One `macOS ARM64 [local]` job failed. It is the same Sandbox E2E guardian error as on #780: `candidate daemon did not become ready; … corrected transition lacks ex…` on Shipyard-studio-02. It also fails on main and is not required.

verdict: HOLD head:cb5c1f796dac6851062af69def634aade161fb1f

READY for re-review: head `fd0e94e25f447578256f3aae97cc0ab6103d5f0c` (read from the API after the push). It is a fast-forward from `cb5c1f79`, contains main `d93317059df589d03b7edad2326b5fe809b1bd02` (merged, not rebased), and is not armed.

This head addresses https://github.com/danielraffel/Shipyard/pull/784#issuecomment-6120093415.

### What changed
- **Ejections come from GitHub's own removal records.** An ejection is a `RemovedFromMergeQueueEvent` by `github-merge-queue` with reason `failed_checks` or `checks_timed_out`; the denominator is `AddedToMergeQueueEvent` entries. Both are dated in the week and read from the timelines of the pull requests the window's merge-group runs name (`gh-readonly-queue/<base>/pr-<n>-<sha>`), plus those merged in it. Every other removal is reported under `merge_queue.removals` by reason and actor.
- **The timeline read is checked against `filteredCount`.** With `itemTypes`, the connection's `totalCount` counts the whole timeline (44 against 4 matching events on #9620), so it cannot be used.
- **The per-run number is its own metric.** It is renamed `merge_group_gate`, the "merge-group gate failure rate", with fields `failures`, `failure_rate`, `gate_failed_rate` and `run_failed_gate_passed`.
- **The report names what each rate judges.** A new `scopes` block covers the should-fix:
  - ejections judge every required check, through GitHub's removal reason;
  - the gate rate judges only `--gate-job` of the workflow in merge-group runs;
  - red after push judges the listed required contexts.
- **Docs.** `--help`, the module docs and the ci/shipyard skills now give these definitions. The ci skill's old line ("a run that failed with its gate green is not an ejection") is replaced with the W41 disagreement numbers.
- **Limitation, stated in the docs.** A queue entry removed before any merge-group run was built for it is seen only if the same pull request has another run in the window. Over a week this is how #9831's `merge_conflict` removal is found; a narrow window can miss such a removal.

### Fixtures (all captured live with the same queries)
| Test | Real data | What it pins |
|---|---|---|
| `pulp_week_41_has_thirty_eight_ejections` | `w41-timelines.json`: the queue timelines of all 470 PRs that W41 reads | 543 entries; **38 ejections** (36 `failed_checks`, 2 `checks_timed_out`); `merge_conflict` 17; `manual` by shipyard-local 27, by github-merge-queue 5, by danielraffel 1; `merged` 455; rate 0.07 |
| `a_window_scores_...` (window a, 10-05 15:00..15:20) | 3 merge-group runs and 7 timelines | 2 gate failures (#9606's group failed, and #9606 stayed queued and merged) against **0 ejections** |
| `an_ejection_while_the_gate_passed_is_counted` (window d, 10-06 14:05..14:15) | run 37476264170 and #9741's timeline | `macos` green, the run failed, and the queue removed #9741 for `failed_checks` 5 minutes later: **1 ejection, 0 gate failures** |
| `a_cancelled_gate_and_a_manual_removal_are_not_ejections` (window e, 10-06 09:30..09:40) | 2 runs, timelines of #9706 and #9724 | #9706's gate was `cancelled_after_start` (1 gate failure), then shipyard-local removed it by hand: **0 ejections**, `manual` by shipyard-local listed |
| `only_the_queue_s_own_check_removals_are_ejections` | compute-level | `failed_checks` by another actor, `manual` by the queue and `merge_conflict` are not ejections |
| `a_short_or_unreadable_timeline_is_refused` | #9741's timeline, cut | short of `filteredCount`, or a removal with no reason, is an error |

### Live run, 2026-09-28..2026-10-12 (release binary, read-only `--no-cache`)
| Week | Entries | Ejections (rate) | Other removals | Gate failures of `macos` / runs | Run failed, gate green |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| W40 | 469 | 24 failed_checks (0.05) | merge_conflict 14; manual: shipyard-local 22, queue 4; merged 404 | 49 / 506 | 274 |
| W41 | 543 | **38**: 36 failed_checks + 2 checks_timed_out (0.07) | merge_conflict 17; manual: shipyard-local 27, queue 5, danielraffel 1; merged 455 | 59 / 603 | 146 |

W41 matches your recompute exactly.

### Checks
m1 has been unreachable over both LAN and Tailscale, so the final verification ran in a disposable Tart VM on m3: a clone of `pulp-build-runner:latest`, rust 1.97.1 installed in the VM, nothing run on bare m3.
- **Tree transfer.** The VM's `--dir` share served a stale copy of a file edited after boot, so I streamed `git ls-files` in over `tart exec` stdin instead. The VM-side `shasum` digest of all 1169 files equals the host's (`a441be8d…`).
- `cargo fmt --all --check` (the toolchain's `cargo-fmt`; the image has no proxy for it): clean.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`: exit 0. The only warning is the known `unknown lint: clippy::assert_is_empty`.
- `cargo test --locked --lib -- gate_cost metrics_gate_cost`: **40 passed, 0 failed**, 19 of them scorecard tests.
- Full suite (`--no-fail-fast`, `RUST_MIN_STACK=32MiB`): **4151 passed, 2 failed.** Both failures shell out to `git ls-files`, and the streamed tree has no `.git`. Now that #785 is in main, none of the earlier gh-auth failures remain.
- Non-Rust pre-push gates, run by hand before pushing with `SHIPYARD_SKIP_PREPUSH=1`: skill_sync 0, version_bump 0, doc_sync 0, include_str 0.

### Mutants on this tree (in the VM)
Each is a non-empty 1/1 diff, run with `cargo test --locked --lib -- gate_cost::scorecard`. Afterwards each was restored with `cmp`, and `diff -rq` showed the tree pristine.

| Mutant | Killing tests |
|---|---|
| Q1: any actor's `failed_checks` ejects | `only_the_queue_s_own_check_removals_are_ejections` |
| Q2: `manual` counts as an ejection | that test, `pulp_week_41_has_thirty_eight_ejections` |
| Q3: rate over all events, not entries | 4 tests incl. W41 and window d |
| Q4: a short timeline read accepted | `a_short_or_unreadable_timeline_is_refused` |
| Q5: a week ignores event dates | 4 tests incl. W41 |
| Q6: a missing reason read as `unknown` | `a_short_or_unreadable_timeline_is_refused` |
| Q7: no PR taken from the queue branch | 5 tests |
| Q8: `checks_timed_out` not an ejection | `only_the_queue_s_own_...`, W41 |
| S4: the run's conclusion stands in for the gate's | 4 tests incl. windows d and e |

Before m1 went down, the 16 earlier S-mutants (S1–S16) were all killed on the previous code on m1, and they are untouched by this change. One mutant of the window filter in `gather` was equivalent to `compute`'s per-week filter, so I removed that code; its replacement, Q5, is killed.

Delta review of head fd0e94e25f447578256f3aae97cc0ab6103d5f0c against my ejection HOLD in issuecomment-6120093415. I read the head from the API before and after this review, and it is not armed. It is a fast-forward from cb5c1f79 that merges main d9331705.

**Independent recompute.** I used my own scripts, reading GitHub's `AddedToMergeQueueEvent` and `RemovedFromMergeQueueEvent` timeline items. For each week I read the PRs named by its `build.yml` merge_group runs, plus the PRs merged in it, and checked each timeline against `filteredCount` with no next page.

| Week | Entries | Ejections (rate) | Other removals |
|---|---|---|---|
| W41 (#784 evidence) | 543 | 38: 36 `failed_checks` + 2 `checks_timed_out` (0.07) | merge_conflict 17; manual: shipyard-local 27, queue 5, danielraffel 1; merged 455 |
| W41 (mine) | **543** | **38** (36 + 2), 0.07 | merge_conflict 17; manual 27 / 5 / 1; merged 455 |
| W40 (#784 evidence) | 469 | 24 `failed_checks` (0.05) | merge_conflict 14; manual 22 / 4; merged 404 |
| W40 (mine, W40-only PR set) | 468 | **24** (0.05) | merge_conflict **13**; manual 22 / 4; merged 404 |
| W40 (mine, the evidence's two-week PR set) | **469** | **24** | merge_conflict **14** |

W41 matches exactly. The single W40 difference is #9510: queued at 2026-10-04T22:00:11Z and removed for `merge_conflict` at 22:54:50Z, with no W40 merge-group run. It is found only because the evidence's run read both weeks at once. That is the limitation the PR documents ("a narrow window can miss such a removal"), and with the same window the counts are identical.

**Fixtures are real.** All 13 `timeline-*.json` fixtures match the live API event for event, comparing type, `createdAt`, reason and the removal actor. That includes #9741 (`failed_checks` by the queue, then merged), #9706 (10 manual removals by shipyard-local, then merged), #9724 and #9620. Run 37476264170's live record agrees with `d-jobs-…`: `head_branch gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-9741-…`, conclusion `failure`, `macos` `success`.

**Mutants** ran in a disposable Tart VM on m3: a clone of `pulp-build-runner:latest`, 6 CPU and 12 GB, with the pinned rust 1.97.1. Nothing ran on bare m3. Each diff was non-empty with a `Compiling shipyard` line, and each file was restored and checked with `cmp`. The command was `cargo test --locked --lib -- gate_cost`; the baseline is **40 passed, 0 failed**.

| Mutant | Result |
|---|---|
| Q1: any actor's `failed_checks` ejects | killed: `only_the_queue_s_own_check_removals_are_ejections` |
| Q2: `manual` added to `EJECTION_REASONS` | killed: that test and `pulp_week_41_has_thirty_eight_ejections` |
| Q3: rate over all events, not entries | killed: 4, incl. W41 and the gate-passed window |
| Q4: a short timeline read accepted | killed: `a_short_or_unreadable_timeline_is_refused` |
| Q5: the week filter ignores event dates | killed: 4, incl. W41 |
| Q7: `checks_timed_out` dropped from `EJECTION_REASONS` | killed: 2, incl. W41 |

**Should-fix:** the fixture narrative for #9741 is inaccurate. The evidence says the queue removed #9741 "5 minutes later" after a run whose `macos` was green. Live timestamps show the removal at **14:12:11Z**, but that run's `macos` started at 14:14:07Z and finished `success` at 14:31:51Z, and its Linux job failed at 14:19:47Z. So the ejection came **before** this run's gate started, and another required context removed it. The test's point still holds: the scorecard counts the ejection from the timeline although the `macos` gate passed. Correct the comment and evidence wording.

**CI on this head.** Linux ×3, Windows ×2, Coverage ×2, Python helper tests ×2, Enforce version & skill sync ×2 and Resolve runners ×3 are all `success`. One `macOS ARM64 [local]` is `success`. The other, 114851854636, is the Sandbox E2E job on Shipyard-studio-02 failing in the M3 guardian steps (`guardian-receipt.json` missing this time). It is environmental and not required.

My ejection HOLD is resolved.

verdict: APPROVE head:fd0e94e25f447578256f3aae97cc0ab6103d5f0c
